claim: A label names a single pocket of ground inside a district rather than the district itself, telling the buyer the fruit came off that one patch. (option "A single vineyard")
because: A registered single vineyard is also a certified origin claim under the scheme. It is a single parcel under 6 ha, so "that one patch" describes it more literally than it describes a ward. A careful candidate could reasonably key option 0 instead of the ward. The scheme's nested geographical tiers are geographical unit, region, district and ward.
fix: Replace option 0 "A single vineyard" with "A geographical unit" (key stays 3), or change the stem ending to "Which geographical tier of the Wine of Origin scheme, demarcated on soil, climate and ecology, is that tighter name?"
